meta.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
meta.author: bank-team-web-development
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.topic: What a component takes responsibility for
questions.stem: An architect's brief asks a component to fetch, format, and render data. Is that ideal?

options.text: Yes, one component can do all

questions.explanation: Separating data fetching from presentation improves reuse and testing. Keep components focused on one responsibility.

questions.topic: One-way data flow when a child edits a value
questions.stem: A child needs to change a parent value. What is the correct pattern?

options.text: Call a callback passed from the parent
Emit an event to the DOM

questions.explanation: Data flows down via props and changes flow up via callbacks. This keeps state ownership clear.

questions.topic: Each render reads a fixed snapshot of state
questions.stem: During a render, state variables reflect which value?

options.misconception: render uses the snapshot at render time
pending updates are not visible yet

options.text: The value at the start of this render

questions.explanation: Each render closes over the state values from that render. Updates create a new render with new values.

questions.topic: Batching the writes made in one event
questions.stem: Three setState calls in one click handler. How many re-renders occur?
questions.explanation: React batches updates in event handlers into a single re-render for efficiency.

questions.topic: Two writes built from a value the render captured
questions.learningObjective: Identify stale state in chained updates
questions.stem: Two setCount(count + 1) calls in one handler add 1 instead of 2. Why?

options.text: Both read the same stale count

questions.explanation: Both updates read the same render snapshot. Use functional updates to chain correctly.

questions.topic: The functional form of a state update
questions.stem: Which update adds 1 reliably when called twice?
questions.explanation: Functional updates receive the latest state, so repeated calls accumulate correctly.

questions.topic: A handler frozen at the render that created it
questions.stem: A handler logged a value from two renders ago. Why?

options.misconception: memoization is not the root cause

options.text: It closed over an old render's variable

questions.explanation: Handlers capture the variables from their creating render. Re-create or use refs to access latest values.

questions.topic: When a memoised child is actually reused
questions.stem: A memoized child re-renders every parent render. Why?

options.misconception: state does not force parent-driven rerender

options.text: Props are new object references each render

questions.explanation: React.memo compares props shallowly. New object or function identities each render defeat it. Stabilize props with useMemo/useCallback.

questions.topic: A stored total that outlives the items it came from
questions.stem: A stored total becomes wrong after items change. What is the cause?

options.text: The total is computed too often
The total is stored state instead of derived

questions.explanation: Storing derived values risks desync. Compute the total from items during render or with useMemo.

questions.topic: Two in-flight requests writing the same state
questions.learningObjective: Handle race conditions in async state
questions.stem: Two fetches resolve out of order and overwrite state with stale data. What is the issue?

options.misconception: speed is not the root cause

questions.explanation: Out-of-order resolutions overwrite newer state with older data. Track the latest request or cancel stale ones.

questions.topic: Which values are inputs and which are consequences
questions.stem: In a component, which value should be a prop rather than state?

options.text: A value computed from another prop
options.misconception: derived values need not be state

options.text: A value passed in from the parent
A value toggled by the user

questions.explanation: Props are inputs from the parent. Derived values should be computed, not stored.

questions.topic: Where shared state belongs in the tree
questions.stem: Two sibling components need the same state. Where should it live?
questions.explanation: Lift state to the common ancestor so both siblings receive it via props and update via callbacks.

questions.topic: A controlled input whose handler stores nothing
questions.stem: A controlled input's onChange does not call setState. What happens?
questions.explanation: A controlled input's value is driven by state. Without updating state, typing has no effect and the field appears frozen.

questions.topic: Fetching and rendering in one component
questions.stem: Fetching and rendering in one component makes testing hard because?

options.text: Network calls run during render tests

questions.explanation: Coupling fetch to render forces tests to mock network. Extract data fetching into a hook or container.

questions.topic: Why a list needs a key that is not its position
questions.stem: Why should list keys not be array indices when items reorder?

options.text: Indices change on reorder, causing state mix-ups

questions.explanation: Index keys are positional. Reordering changes which data maps to which instance, mixing state.

questions.topic: An effect that subscribes and never unsubscribes
questions.stem: An effect subscribes to a store but never unsubscribes. What leaks?

options.text: A subscription and possible duplicate updates

questions.explanation: Missing cleanup leaves dangling subscriptions, causing memory leaks and duplicate updates. Return a cleanup function.

questions.topic: Reading a value before and after a batched handler
questions.stem: A handler calls setState then logs state. What does it log?
questions.explanation: State updates are queued; the current closure still sees the old value until the next render.

questions.topic: Counting effect runs from a dependency list
questions.stem: An effect has deps [a, b]. How many times does it run when a changes twice?
questions.explanation: The effect runs after mount and whenever a dependency changes. Two changes in a means two runs plus mount.
questions.hint: Each dep change triggers a run.

questions.topic: Why a stored derived value eventually disagrees with its input
questions.stem: A stored derived value drifts from its source. Why?

options.text: The derived value is too fast
Updates to the source do not update the derived copy

questions.explanation: Storing derived state creates a second source of truth. Compute on render to stay in sync.

questions.topic: The path from a click to a repaint
questions.stem: What is the path from a click to a repaint?

options.text: Click -> state update -> render -> commit -> paint

questions.explanation: Events update state, React renders, commits changes to the DOM, then the browser paints.

questions.topic: One variable shared by every turn of a loop
questions.stem: A for loop with var creates callbacks that all use the final index. Why?
questions.explanation: var has function scope, so all closures share one binding. Use let for block scope.

questions.topic: The one rule a custom hook must obey
questions.stem: What is the one rule a custom hook must obey?

options.misconception: custom hooks should start with use

options.text: Call hooks only at the top level

questions.explanation: Hooks must be called at the top level of the component or custom hook, never in conditions or loops.

questions.topic: Passing a value through components that ignore it
questions.stem: Passing a value through components that ignore it is called?
questions.explanation: Prop drilling passes data through intermediate components. Use context or composition to avoid it.

questions.topic: When one reducer is better than local state
questions.stem: When is useReducer better than multiple useState?

options.text: When state is a single boolean
When state transitions are complex and interdependent

questions.explanation: Reducers centralize complex transition logic. Simple independent values suit useState.

questions.topic: Reading a parameter out of an address
questions.stem: A route /users/:id. How to read id in the component?
questions.explanation: useParams returns route parameters. Query strings use useSearchParams.

questions.topic: A nested route and the outlet it renders into
questions.stem: In a nested route, where does the child render?
questions.explanation: The parent renders an Outlet placeholder where matched child routes render.

questions.topic: What an error boundary does and does not catch
questions.stem: What does an error boundary NOT catch?

options.misconception: it may not catch async errors

questions.explanation: Error boundaries catch render errors, not event handler errors. Handle those with try/catch.

questions.topic: What a context value change reaches
questions.stem: When a context value changes, which components re-render?

options.text: Only components that consume that context

questions.explanation: Context updates re-render all consumers of that context. Non-consumers are unaffected.

questions.topic: An answer that arrives after the request was abandoned
questions.stem: A fetch resolves after the component unmounted. What can happen?

options.text: A state update on an unmounted component

questions.explanation: Resolving after unmount can update state on an unmounted component. Use an ignore flag or AbortController.

questions.topic: A callback kept for the sake of being stable
questions.stem: Why wrap a callback in useCallback?

options.text: To keep its identity stable across renders

questions.explanation: useCallback returns a memoized function identity, preserving referential equality across renders.

questions.topic: Applying a sequence of actions to a reducer
questions.stem: A reducer handles INCREMENT and DECREMENT. Starting at 0, dispatch INCREMENT then DECREMENT. Result?
questions.explanation: Each action updates state from the previous result: 0 + 1 - 1 = 0.

questions.topic: Memoising a component whose props keep changing
questions.stem: React.memo on a component whose props change every render. Effect?

options.misconception: memo does not skip on changed props

questions.explanation: React.memo only skips when props are shallowly equal. Changing props every render means no skipping.

questions.topic: Two requests sharing one loading flag
questions.stem: Two requests share one isLoading flag. What goes wrong?

options.text: One finishing clears loading while the other is still pending

questions.explanation: A shared flag is cleared by whichever request finishes first, hiding the other's pending state. Use per-request flags.

questions.topic: A claim the dependency list contradicts
questions.stem: An effect uses value but deps are empty. What is the bug?
questions.explanation: Missing dependencies make the effect capture the initial value forever. Add all used values to deps.

questions.topic: Counting the two kinds of consumer after a context change
questions.stem: A context change occurs. Which components re-render?

options.text: Components calling useContext for that context

questions.explanation: Only components that consume the changed context re-render. Others are unaffected.

questions.topic: Reading the state a sequence of actions leaves
questions.stem: Reducer starts {count:0}. Actions: add 2, multiply by 3. Final count?
questions.explanation: 0 + 2 = 2, then 2 * 3 = 6. Apply each action in sequence.

questions.topic: The reach of an error boundary
questions.stem: An error boundary catches errors from which components?
questions.explanation: Error boundaries catch errors thrown by their descendant components during render.

questions.topic: The path from a link to a new screen
questions.stem: Clicking a Link changes the URL and renders?
questions.explanation: Client-side routing updates the URL and renders the matched route without a full page reload.

questions.topic: What a router link avoids
questions.stem: Using a router Link instead of an anchor avoids what?
questions.explanation: A router Link performs client-side navigation, avoiding a full page reload and preserving app state.

questions.topic: What a server-rendered component cannot do
questions.stem: What can a server component NOT do?
questions.explanation: Server components run on the server and cannot access browser APIs. Use client components for those.

questions.topic: What a component takes responsibility for
questions.stem: How should a component's responsibility be defined?

answer.exemplar: A component should do one thing well, such as rendering a view or managing one piece of state, and delegate the rest.

questions.explanation: Focused components are easier to test, reuse, and maintain. Split mixed concerns.

questions.topic: One-way data flow when a child edits a value
questions.stem: A child input changes a parent value. Which code is correct?
questions.explanation: Controlled input with a change handler calling the parent's setter implements one-way data flow.

questions.topic: Each render reads a fixed snapshot of state
questions.stem: Inside render, you log count then call setCount(count+1). What is logged?
questions.explanation: The log uses the value from this render's snapshot. The update applies in the next render.

questions.topic: Batching the writes made in one event
questions.stem: A click handler calls setA(1), setB(2), setC(3). How many renders?
questions.explanation: React batches the three updates into a single re-render in the event handler.

questions.topic: Two writes built from a value the render captured
questions.stem: Fix two increments in one handler. Which code adds 2?
questions.explanation: Functional updates receive the latest state, so two calls add 2.

questions.topic: The functional form of a state update
questions.stem: Why use the functional form of setState?

answer.exemplar: It receives the latest state, avoiding stale snapshots when updates are batched or chained.

questions.explanation: Functional updates guarantee the previous state is current, preventing lost updates in batches.

questions.topic: A handler frozen at the render that created it
questions.stem: A useEffect with [] logs an old prop. How to fix?
questions.explanation: Include the used prop in the dependency array so the effect re-runs with the latest value.

questions.topic: When a memoised child is actually reused
questions.stem: A memoized child gets a new object prop each render. Fix?
questions.explanation: useMemo keeps the object identity stable across renders, letting React.memo skip.

questions.topic: A stored total that outlives the items it came from
questions.stem: Instead of storing total, how to compute it?

options.text: Store total and update on add

questions.explanation: Derive the total from items during render so it always matches.

questions.topic: Two in-flight requests writing the same state
questions.stem: How to ignore a stale fetch result?

options.text: Use an ignore flag set on cleanup

questions.explanation: Set a flag on cleanup and check it before updating state. Or use AbortController.

questions.topic: Which values are inputs and which are consequences
questions.stem: A component receives userId and computes userName. Which is state?
questions.explanation: userName derived from userId can be state if fetched, but ideally compute or fetch. userId is a prop.

questions.topic: Where shared state belongs in the tree
questions.stem: Two siblings need shared state. Where to put it?
questions.explanation: Lift state to the common parent and pass down via props with callbacks.

questions.topic: A controlled input whose handler stores nothing
questions.stem: A controlled input does not update. What is missing?
questions.explanation: Controlled inputs need an onChange that updates state, otherwise the value never changes.

questions.topic: Fetching and rendering in one component
questions.stem: How to separate fetching from rendering?

answer.exemplar: Extract data fetching into a custom hook or container component, and pass data down to a presentational component.

questions.explanation: Separation improves testability and reuse. Presentational components stay pure.
questions.hint: Extract to a hook or container.

questions.topic: Why a list needs a key that is not its position
questions.stem: A list of users can reorder. Which key is best?
questions.explanation: Use a stable unique id. Index and random keys cause state mix-ups.

questions.topic: An effect that subscribes and never unsubscribes
questions.stem: An effect adds an event listener. What must it return?

options.text: A cleanup that removes the listener

questions.explanation: Return a cleanup function that removes the listener to prevent leaks.

questions.topic: Reading a value before and after a batched handler
questions.stem: State read immediately after setState in the same handler is?
questions.explanation: The update is queued; the current closure still sees the old value until the next render.

questions.topic: Counting effect runs from a dependency list
questions.stem: An effect with deps [x] runs on mount and when x changes. If x changes 3 times, total runs?
questions.explanation: One mount run plus three change runs equals four total runs.

questions.topic: Why a stored derived value eventually disagrees with its input
questions.stem: A stored derived value is stale. Root cause?

options.text: The derived value is too slow
The source changed but derived was not updated

questions.explanation: Storing derived state creates a second source of truth that can desync. Compute on render.

questions.topic: The path from a click to a repaint
questions.stem: Which sequence is correct for a click updating UI?
questions.explanation: State update triggers render, commit applies DOM changes, then the browser paints.
